````markdown
# PL × sector-overview — the highest gross margin in the universe, at −37% operating

## The finding

**PL holds the best gross margin in this universe — 53.5% — and the operating line is −37.06%.**
Both are DEMONSTRATED and both are filed. The 90.5 percentage-point gap between them is the
value-chain finding: **PL is the cleanest available test of "which position in the stack holds the
margin", and the answer is that the position holding the gross margin is not the position holding
the operating margin, because the fixed cost base is set independently of the gross margin level.**

Three consequences, and they are the substance:

1. **The loss is a FIXED-COST result, not a launch-cost result.** Cost of revenue is **46.5%** of
   revenue; operating expenses are **90.6%** of revenue and **1.692× gross profit**. Launch cost
   lives inside the 46.5% and is demonstrably not the binding constraint — **PL retains 53.5%
   gross while absorbing it.** This is evidence *for* PIL-6's migration claim and against reading
   launch cost as the sector's value variable.
2. **Operating leverage is NEGATIVE.** Revenue grew **+42%** and the loss from operations widened
   **+53%**; opex grew **+44%**, faster than revenue. `[📄 PL 10-Q p.38](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/38)`
   A 42% growth quarter produced a wider loss. There is no scale fix at this revenue level.
3. **76.7% of the net loss is a non-operating warrant remeasurement** — a DA-24 contamination
   point that must be quantified, not netted. `[📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6)`

## 1. Component identity, opex definition, units

**Opex definition: total operating expenses as filed — R&D, sales and marketing, and general and
administrative — EXCLUSIVE of cost of revenue.** PL files a **gross-profit line**, so both pairings
are computable, and this is the one issuer in this cohort where they agree.

| Pairing | Arithmetic ($k) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Exclusive** (filed lines) | 50,401 − 85,289 | **(34,888)** ✓ |
| **Inclusive** (cost of revenue added to opex) | 94,150 − (43,749 + 85,289) | **(34,888)** ✓ |

**Both pairings give the same answer, and the reason is worth stating because it is not a
coincidence.** The inclusive pairing uses `revenue − cost_of_revenue − opex`; the exclusive uses
`gross_profit − opex`; and `revenue − cost_of_revenue = gross_profit` **by the filer's own
arithmetic**. They converge **precisely because the gross-profit line exists**. At GSAT, IRDM and
YSS the first term is unavailable or the second is misfiled, and the two definitions diverge by
the entire cost of sales. **So the opex-definition ambiguity is a defect of the issuers who do not
file a gross-profit line, not of the concept.** `[📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6)`

**Full statement, quarter ended 2026-04-30 vs the quarter ended 2025-04-30:**

| Line ($k) | 2026-04-30 | 2025-04-30 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **94,150** | 66,265 | **+42.08%** |
| Cost of revenue | 43,749 | 29,662 | +47.49% |
| **Gross profit** | **50,401** | 36,603 | **+37.70%** |
| **Gross margin** | **53.53%** | 55.24% | **−1.71pp** |
| Research and development | 33,420 | 23,074 | +44.84% |
| Sales and marketing | 22,782 | 16,314 | +39.65% |
| General and administrative | 29,087 | 19,986 | +45.54% |
| **Total operating expenses** | **85,289** | 59,374 | **+43.65%** |
| **Loss from operations** | **(34,888)** | (22,771) | **+53.21%** |
| **Operating margin** | **−37.06%** | −34.36% | **−2.70pp** |
| Interest income | 5,153 | 1,884 | — |
| Interest expense | (1,446) | (499) | — |
| **Change in fair value of warrant liabilities** | **(106,474)** | 10,387 | — |
| Total other income (expense), net | (102,973) | 11,071 | — |
| Loss before income taxes | (137,861) | (11,700) | — |
| **Net loss** | **(138,872)** | (12,628) | — |
| **EPS** | **$(0.40)** | $(0.04) | — |

**The identity closes exactly:** `50,401 − 85,289 = (34,888)` ✓

**The four ratios that carry the section:**

| Ratio | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Cost of revenue ÷ revenue | **46.47%** | 43,749 / 94,150 |
| Opex ÷ revenue | **90.59%** | 85,289 / 94,150 |
| **Opex ÷ gross profit** | **1.692×** | 85,289 / 50,401 |
| Opex less gross profit | **$34,888k** | the operating loss, exactly |

**Opex exceeds gross profit by exactly the operating loss, which is the identity restated. The
information is in the RATIO: 1.692×.** A fixed cost base 69% larger than gross profit cannot be
covered by any plausible gross-margin improvement at this revenue level — **a 5pp gross-margin gain
would add $4,708k against a $34,888k gap.**

### 1.1 DA-23 at PL — the UNIFORM regime

Every served `OperatingIncomeLoss` at PL is positive and every filed one negative, across the
issuer's entire history — **≥12 periods, all stripped**: quarter ended 2026-04-30 served
**+34,888,000** against filed `(34,888)`; quarter ended 2025-04-30 **+22,771,000**; FY ending
2026-01-31 **+95,073,000**; FY ending 2025-01-31 **+116,122,000**; nine months FY2026
**+59,071,000**; Q3 FY2026 **+18,340,000**; six months FY2026 **+40,731,000**; Q2 FY2026
**+17,960,000**; nine months FY2025 **+96,756,000**; Q3 FY2025 **+22,608,000**; Q2 FY2025
**+39,577,000**; six months FY2025 **+74,148,000**.

**The regime is UNIFORM, so the strip is UNDETECTABLE arithmetically.** Because PL has never had a
positive operating income, the served `|x|` stack is **monotone and internally consistent** — Q2
FY2026 +17,960 ≤ six months +40,731 ≤ nine months +59,071 ≤ FY +95,073. The monotonicity detector
that fires at GSAT **cannot fire here**, exactly as at RKLB and YSS. **The component identity is
the only detector, and it requires reading the filing.** `[📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6)`

### 1.2 ⚠️ Cite the period, never the label — DA-27

**PL's fiscal year ends January 31, so the quarter ended 2026-04-30 is Q1 FY2027.** The platform's
outline for the same document labels the same table **both "Q1 FY2027" and "Q1 FY2026"**, and the
003 entity map calls it **"Q1 FY2026"**. **Three labels, one period.** DA-27 is a label derived
from the calendar quarter rather than the fiscal one, and PL is its live instance.

**Every period in this artifact is therefore cited by period-end date.** A reader who inherits
"Q1 FY2026" from the entity map and compares it against a calendar-year peer is comparing
different quarters, and nothing in the label signals it.

**Units.** As-filed statements are in **thousands**; the platform's `value_numeric` is in
**dollars**. The 1,000× offset is systematic and is a unit conversion, not a defect.

## 2. The GAAP and non-GAAP bases must never be one series

`[📄 PL 10-Q p.41](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/41)`

| Metric | 2026-04-30 | 2025-04-30 |
|---|---|---|
| Gross margin (as filed) | **54%** | 55% |
| Non-GAAP gross margin | **56%** | 59% |
| Non-GAAP gross profit ($k) | 52,968 | 38,850 |
| **Adjusted EBITDA ($k)** | **(1,033)** | 1,199 |

**Two bases on one metric, 2pp apart, and the gap WIDENED from 4pp to 2pp** — i.e. the non-GAAP
adjustment shrank as a share, while the non-GAAP margin fell **3pp** against the GAAP margin's
**1pp**. **The non-GAAP series is deteriorating faster than the GAAP series**, which is the
opposite of what a non-GAAP presentation usually signals. And **Adjusted EBITDA crossed from
positive to negative**: **+$1,199k → $(1,033)k**. A non-GAAP measure that goes negative is the
adjustment's own verdict on the fixed cost base.

**Never quote "PL's gross margin is 54%" and "56%" interchangeably.** Both are filed; they are
different metrics; DA-30.

### 2.1 DA-24 — the net loss is 76.7% a warrant mark

**Change in fair value of warrant liabilities: $(106,474)k** against a **$(138,872)k** net loss =
**76.66%**. `[📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6)`

This is a **non-cash remeasurement of a liability**, and it went the wrong way in the same quarter
the prior-year comparison went the right way (+$10,387k). **The comparison is therefore dominated
by a swing in a non-operating, non-cash item**, and a reader comparing net losses year over year
is comparing two different things. **The operating line is the comparable one, and it is also
worse — `(34,888)` against `(22,771)`.** That matters: **the honest reading is that the operating
deterioration is real *and* the net-loss blowout is mostly non-operating.** Both, not either.

## 3. The value-chain position map

**The purpose of this skill is to locate which position in the stack holds the margin. PL sits one
layer above launch, and it is the strongest available test.**

| Layer | Name | Gross margin | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | RKLB | — (see the RKLB artifact) | deeply negative |
| **Data and analytics, above launch** | **PL** | **53.53%** | **−37.06%** |
| Vertical / infrastructure services | YSS | 23.97% | −44.64% |

**The finding is what happens between the columns.** PL and YSS differ by **29.6 percentage points**
of gross margin and by only **7.6 percentage points** of operating margin. **Gross margin does not
predict operating margin in this sector, and the reason is arithmetic rather than narrative:** PL's
opex ratio is **90.59%** of revenue; YSS's is **68.60%**. **PL's 29.6pp gross-margin advantage is
more than consumed by a 22.0pp higher opex ratio.** The ranking between two names at different
depths of the stack is set by the fixed cost base, not by the position.

**And that is the answer to the sector-overview question, stated precisely: in this stack, at these
two names, NO position holds an operating margin, and the value-chain depth of a name tells you
nothing about which of them loses less.** A map that ranks positions by gross margin produces the
exact inverse of a map that ranks them by operating margin.

### 3.1 Where launch cost actually sits in PL's cost structure

**Launch is inside PL's 46.47% cost of revenue, and PL retains 53.53% gross while paying it.**
That is the load-bearing inference for PIL-6:

- **If launch cost were the binding constraint at the data layer, a data-layer gross margin of
  53.53% would not be available.** It is.
- **Therefore the constraint at the data layer is not launch cost.** It is the **90.59% opex
  ratio** — R&D at **35.50%** of revenue, sales and marketing at **24.20%**, G&A at **30.90%**.
- **So the value did not stay at the launch layer, and it did not stop at the data layer either.**
  It migrated upward and was consumed by the fixed cost of operating a data business at sub-scale
  revenue. **PIL-2's "value migrated to the integrator that owns the demand" is confirmed in
  direction and refined in destination: the migration is real and the destination is a cost base,
  not a margin.**

**PL's own risk set confirms the reading.** A filed risk factor is **"history of operating
losses"** `[📄 PL 10-Q p.47](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/47)`, and the other filed exposures are
**competition** (p.49), **satellite development and launch** (p.51), **supply chain and cloud**
(p.59), **customer concentration and seasonality** (p.62), **NOAA/FCC/ITAR/EAR/OFAC regulatory**
(p.77) and the **2030 Notes and capped calls** (p.87). **Launch appears once, as a development
dependency. It does not appear as a cost driver anywhere in PL's risk set** — while the fixed cost
components (cloud, personnel-driven G&A, and the debt service) appear repeatedly. **The filer's own
risk taxonomy ranks launch below the fixed cost base as a threat to the business.** That is a
`CLAIMED`-grade filing statement and it agrees with the DEMONSTRATED arithmetic in §1.

### 3.2 The growth is real and it is concentrated

Revenue grew **+$27,885k / +42.08%**, driven by a **$24.7M increase in the defense and intelligence
vertical.** `[📄 PL 10-Q p.38](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/38)`

**$24.7M of a $27,885k increase is 88.6% — one vertical.** That is not diversification; it is
single-account growth against a filed **customer-concentration-and-seasonality** risk factor
(p.62). **The margin consequence is adverse**: defense and intelligence revenue carries a different
cost structure than imagery subscription revenue, and the **cost of revenue grew +47.49% against
revenue +42.08%** — i.e. **the growth is arriving at a worse incremental gross margin than the
existing base**, which is why the gross margin fell 1.71pp even in a 42% growth quarter.
**Growth is diluting the gross margin and widening the operating loss simultaneously.**

## 5. What this artifact could not resolve

- **`UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES` — PL's launch cost.** Inside cost of revenue, not
  separately disclosed at any granularity. The resolving disclosure is a cost-of-revenue
  decomposition naming launch.
- **`UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES` — the defense-and-intelligence vertical's own margin.** The
  $24.7M is named as the growth driver; its gross margin is not disclosed, so the **dilution claim
  in §3.2 is inferred from the blended cost-of-revenue growth (+47.49%) and NOT from a segment
  margin.** Stated as an inference, not as a filed figure.
- **`UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES` — the fixed cost base's scale-invariant share.** R&D,
  sales and marketing and G&A all grew **+39.7% to +45.5%** against revenue **+42.1%** — near
  proportionality, which is why the loss widened. **The disclosure that would separate fixed from
  variable cost inside opex does not exist**, so "fixed cost" here is characterised by its
  *behaviour* (opex ÷ revenue held at ~90%), not by a filed fixed/variable split.
- **UNEXERCISED — whether the warrant remeasurement can recur.** The $(106,474)k swing is filed
  for this quarter; the warrant terms that would bound future marks were not read.
- **UNEXERCISED — the 2030 Notes' covenants and the capped calls.** The risk factor exists at
  p.87; the terms were not read.
- **NOT ATTEMPTED — DA-28, DA-29.** No share-count detector is asserted (DA-28); no reconciliation
  is claimed whose terms are absent from the source (DA-29). **Recorded as not attempted. Not
  attempted is not CLEAN.**
- **`get_segment_data` UNUSABLE** (`column "k" does not exist`; double-counts) and
  **`data_freshness` UNUSABLE** (returns `2027-04-12`, seven months in the future of
  `as_of = 2026-09-18`). **Pages read directly.**
````

````markdown
# PL — the margin ladder, the served-sign defect, and the demand-side programme-cost shares

**Finding.** Planet Labs files a **53.5% gross margin** — the highest in this thesis's universe — against an
operating margin of **−37.1%** and a net margin of **−147.5%**. The company is not a launch-cost story at all:
its filed demand-side programme-cost commitment to *reach orbit* is **$4.7 million**, while its commitment to
*process the data* is **$58,545 thousand** — a ratio of **12.5× against launch**. PL therefore contributes a
**negative** result to PIL-6, and it is a sharp one: at the payload-integrator end of the value chain, the
binding programme cost is not the rocket. Separately, PL is **DA-23's cleanest instance in the universe**,
because the gross-profit bound test is **silent** here (P5).

## 1. Acceptance test — adopted and run

Every identification below is accepted only if it is **(a) exact**, **(b) stable across periods**, and
**(c) consistent with a specified formula or a filed basis**. Anything else is recorded `UNRESOLVED` — never
"probably fine". This test is not decorative: the register records a ~**2,500**-candidate sweep over **36 filed
cells** that produced **6–9 coincidental hits per metric**, and only **2 of 16** served ratio fields were the
ratio they claimed. **Every ratio in this artifact is recomputed from filed cells; no served ratio is quoted.**
`list_xbrl_concepts(search="ratio")` returns **no margin concept in the served layer**, so at PL there is nothing
to quote even in principle.

Formula for every margin below: `ratio = filed numerator ÷ filed denominator`, both read off a single filed page.

## 2. The margin ladder

All figures in $ thousands. Both columns are read from one page.

| Line | Q1 FY2027 | Q1 FY2026 | Basis | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 94,150 | 66,265 | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| Cost of revenue | 43,749 | 29,662 | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| **Gross profit** | **50,401** | **36,603** | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| R&D | 33,420 | 23,074 | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| Sales & marketing | 22,782 | 16,314 | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| General & administrative | 29,087 | 19,986 | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |
| **Total operating expenses** | **85,289** | **59,374** | the three lines above, summed | DEMONSTRATED |
| **Loss from operations** | **(34,888)** | **(22,771)** | filed, parenthesised | DEMONSTRATED |
| Net loss | (138,872) | (12,628) | consolidated, as filed | DEMONSTRATED |

Source: [📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6)

**The opex definition used here is the EXCLUSIVE one** — R&D + S&M + G&A only, i.e. the three operating-expense
lines printed below gross profit. This matters: `us-gaap:CostsAndExpenses` **includes** cost of sales, so the
component identity is false wherever a cost-of-sales line exists. At PL a cost-of-revenue line does exist, so
the inclusive pairing is inadmissible.

**Component identity, run on four periods:**

```
Q1 FY2027:  50,401 − 85,289  = (34,888)   exact
Q1 FY2026:  36,603 − 59,374  = (22,771)   exact
FY2026:    172,485 − 267,558 = (95,073)   exact
FY2025:    139,725 − 255,847 = (116,122)  exact
```

Annual lines from [📄 PL 10-K p.78](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/78). All four close to the dollar. This is the
**only** reliable sign detector, and PL is the case that demonstrates why.

### 2.1 Derived ratios

| Ratio | Q1 FY2027 | Q1 FY2026 | Formula | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gross margin | **53.53%** | 55.24% | gross profit ÷ revenue | DEMONSTRATED |
| Operating margin | **−37.06%** | −34.36% | loss from operations ÷ revenue | DEMONSTRATED |
| Opex ratio | **90.59%** | 89.60% | total opex ÷ revenue | DEMONSTRATED |
| **Opex ÷ gross profit** | **1.692×** | 1.622× | total opex ÷ gross profit | DEMONSTRATED |
| Net margin | −147.50% | −19.06% | net loss ÷ revenue | DEMONSTRATED |
| Cost of revenue growth | **+47%** | — | filed % change column | DEMONSTRATED |
| Revenue growth | +42% | — | filed % change column | DEMONSTRATED |

The filed % change column is at [📄 PL 10-Q p.38](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/38). **Cost of revenue grew 47%
against revenue growth of 42%** — margin compression of **1.71 percentage points**, filed as such. The ladder's
shape is: a genuinely high gross margin, entirely consumed by a fixed cost base running at **1.69× gross
profit**. On the FY2026/FY2025 pair the same structure holds: gross margin **56.05% → 57.18%**, i.e.
**172,485 ÷ 307,727 = 56.05%** (filed **56%**) and **139,725 ÷ 244,352 = 57.18%** (filed **57%**), both at
[📄 PL 10-K p.82](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/82). **PL's gross margin is one of the ratios that IS the ratio
it claims** — it reproduces from filed cells to the rounded percent. That is a positive result and it is stated
as one.

## 3. P5 — DA-23 at PL is the cleanest instance in the universe, because the bound test is silent

**Every served `OperatingIncomeLoss` value in the PL fact set is POSITIVE.** The served window spans **18
distinct fiscal periods from FY2024 Q1 (2024-02-01→2024-04-30) to FY2027 Q1 (2026-02-01→2026-04-30)**, and no
negative value appears anywhere in it. Values include `+34,888,000`, `+95,073,000`, `+116,122,000`,
`+22,771,000`, `+169,748,000`, `+135,830,000`. Grade: DEMONSTRATED, from the served layer — which is exactly
where DA-23 lives.

**The filed pages print every one of those with parentheses.** The four periods reconciled above are filed as
`(34,888)`, `(22,771)`, `(95,073)`, `(116,122)` — at [📄 PL 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/6) and
[📄 PL 10-K p.78](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/78). Same magnitude, opposite sign. That is DA-23's definition:
**absolute-value stripping, not inversion.**

**Why PL is the cleanest instance.** The naive bound test is: *a positive operating income cannot exceed gross
profit.* At PL the served value **+34,888 is BELOW filed gross profit 50,401**, so the bound **does not fire**.
The strip is invisible to it. At YSS — the sibling artifact — the bound *does* fire, because that served value
exceeds its gross profit. So the detector that works at one issuer is silent at another, on the same defect,
in the same register. **The component identity is the only detector that runs at PL**, and §2 shows it closing
exactly on all four periods. `EPS × shares` is **not** an admissible sign test and was not used.

## 4. P6 — DA-24 and DA-30 in the segment table

PL files **one operating and reportable segment** whose table runs all the way to consolidated net loss
([📄 PL 10-K p.146](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/146)). Two register classes fire there.

**DA-24 — non-operating contamination, disclosed rather than hidden.** The table's `Other segment items` line is
footnoted: *"Includes interest income, change in fair value of warrant liabilities, other income (expense), net
and provision for income taxes."* The identification satisfies all three legs of the acceptance test:

```
−interest income          −14,329
+warrant FV change        +161,400
+other income (expense)    −3,375
+income tax provision      +4,655
                          ─────────
                           148,351   = filed "other segment items"   exact
```

**Exact**, consistent with the footnoted formula, and reproducible in FY2025 (**6,242**) and FY2024 by the same
construction. Note FY2024's value is **$(29,239)$ — negative**, a *negative expense* bucket. A sign-strip in
that cell would be undetectable from the value alone; the segment table's own reconciliation to
`Consolidated net loss` is the check that constrains it.

**The magnitude is the finding.** The warrant fair-value change is **$161,400 thousand — 10.4× the entire
Adjusted EBITDA the reconciliation produces.** This is a pre-IPO instrument (DA-28 shape): the share count is
not used as a detector anywhere in this artifact, and the same discipline applies to the warrant liability.

**DA-30 — two filed bases on one concept.** Cost of revenue is filed at **$135,242k** on the income statement
and at **$94,138k** in the segment table. The table's footnote (1) explains the segment figure is *"exclusive of
… depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, restructuring costs …"*. Difference: **$41,104k**.
Both numbers are correct; **neither is comparable to the other**, and neither carries a basis label in the
served layer. **Every cost-of-revenue figure in this artifact therefore names its basis.** The same split
applies to R&D (106,749 vs 80,251), S&M (72,676 vs 63,591) and G&A (88,133 vs 54,252).

## 5. DA-29 — four reconciliations that close, with every term located

DA-29 warns that *a reconciliation that closes is not thereby a check*. The test is whether its terms appear
**in the source**. At PL four reconciliations close exactly **and** name every term on a filed page:

| Reconciliation | Closes to | All terms filed? | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Component identity (4 periods) | the dollar | Yes | p.6, p.78 |
| Non-GAAP gross profit bridge | 182,617 / 147,517 | Yes — 6,881 + 2,933 + 15 + 303 = 10,132 | p.82 |
| Adjusted EBITDA bridge | 15,495 / (10,627) | Yes — 11 terms, all on the page | p.82 |
| Segment table → consolidated net loss | (246,860) | Yes — 11 lines sum exactly | p.146 |

**DA-29 is SATISFIED at PL, four times over** — not merely untriggered. This is the positive inverse of the
register's own warning and it is stated because an unengaged check is not a passed check.

**Adjusted EBITDA is positive: $15,495 thousand in FY2026.** The bridge closes, so the number is arithmetically
sound — but its single largest input is the **$161,400k warrant remeasurement**, a non-operating, non-cash item
that is 10.4× the metric it produces. PL's one positive "profitability" figure is a capital-structure artefact.

## 6. PIL-6 — the demand side does not price off the cost curve

PL **buys** launches; it does not sell them. It therefore contributes **no point to the cost curve** — and that
is a result, not a gap.

Its Note 8 programme commitments ([📄 PL 10-Q p.20](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/20)) put the two sides of its
demand-side cost in one place:

| Commitment | Amount | Window | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch services (third-party) | **$4.7 million** | FY ending 2028 | DEMONSTRATED |
| Google hosting | **$58,545 thousand** | remainder FY2027 + FY2028 | DEMONSTRATED |
| **Hosting ÷ launch** | **12.5×** | — | DEMONSTRATED |

`58,545 ÷ 4,700 = 12.457 → 12.5×`. Exact, formula-consistent, and stable — the hosting line is a two-period
schedule, so the ratio is reproducible from the table rather than from a single cell.

The complementary filed statement is at [📄 PL 10-Q p.11](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec76/11): *"The Company
contracts with certain third-party service providers to launch satellites. **Service providers who provide these
services are limited.**"* PL is a price-taker on launch with a thin supplier set — and still spends **12.5×**
more on hosting than on reaching orbit. **At the payload-integrator end of the chain, the rocket is not the
binding programme cost.** For PIL-6's claim that *the demand side does not price off the curve*, this is
confirming evidence from the demand side itself.

**Capex corroborates the direction of spend:** $81.5M / $49.6M / $42.4M for FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024
([📄 PL 10-K p.146](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/146)) — **+64.3%** in the latest year — filed as *"Capital
Expenditures as a Percentage of Revenue: 26% vs 20%"* at [📄 PL 10-K p.75](https://agentii.ai/v/PL/sec60/75).
Recomputed: **81.5 ÷ 307.727 = 26.49% → 26%** and **49.6 ÷ 244.352 = 20.30% → 20%**. Both reproduce. Capital is
going into satellites and ground segment, not into launch.

|---|---|---|---|
| PL's position on the cost curve | PL files **no** per-launch price, per-launch cost, launch count, or mass-to-orbit — in any period | `UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES` | A per-launch cost or a kg-to-orbit metric in a filed table, on a DA-01-named basis |
| DA-25 at PL | No normalised per-unit metric is filed at all | `UNEXERCISED` — **not** `CLEAN` | Any filed per-unit metric | 
| The FY2024 negative "other segment items" sign | A negative expense bucket is a DA-23-shaped hazard that the served layer cannot rule out from the value alone | `UNRESOLVED` | A quarter-level segment table where the sign is constrained by a second line |

**DA-25 is `UNEXERCISED`, not `CLEAN`.** PL files no normalised per-unit metric, so the check could not run. An
unengaged check is not a passed check, and recording it as clean would be the exact failure mode DA-29 warns
about.

**`UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES`, not `FROM-PLATFORM`.** The missing quantity is absent from the filings
themselves, not from the extraction. Re-querying the platform will not produce it.
````

````markdown
# RKLB × unit-economics — DA-01 A/A′/B/C, the F5c floor, and the RECONVERSION of the measured point

**RKLB is the curve's only measured point. It is also a `P11` deal security — `deal_security_basis:
standalone_pre_merger`, RKLB as acquirer of Iridium (announced 2026-06-29, close expected
mid-2027). Every figure below is pre-merger standalone and none of it absorbs Iridium.**

## 0. The finding

**001's published Electron figures — basis A `$30,333/kg` and basis B `$14,667/kg` — are not
wrong arithmetic. They are a construction on a CEILING, and the ceiling is the only payload mass
RKLB files. They are therefore FLOORS of the true $/kg, and the register's "1.79×–2.62× too low,
four of four periods" is the wrong magnitude and the wrong period count.**

Three results, in order of load:

1. **The RECONVERSION.** The filing files exactly one payload mass — *"launch services into low
   earth orbit on Electron for spacecraft up to 300 kg"* and *"capable of deploying spacecraft of
   up to 300 kg to low Earth orbit across a wide range of orbital inclinations from 38 to 120
   degrees from our operational LC-1 … and … 38 to 60 degrees from our operational LC-2"*
   ([📄 RKLB 10-K p.7](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/7);
   [📄 RKLB 10-K p.8](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/8)) — and it is a **ceiling**, twice stated as
   `up to`. RKLB files **no mass-to-orbit metric in any period**. The one realized-denominator
   adjustment the filing *does* support is the **HASTE mission mix**: two of the six Electron
   missions completed in Q2 2026 were Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron missions
   ([📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37)), which deliver **zero kg to LEO**
   while sitting inside both the revenue and the launch-count numerator. Excluding them from the
   kilogram denominator only:

   | Period | denominator | basis A (revenue) | basis B (cost) | reconv. factor |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | **Q2 2026** | 4 orbital of 6 × 300 kg = **200 kg** | **$45,500/kg** | **$22,000/kg** | **1.50×** |
   | Q2 2026, ceiling (001's inherited value) | 6 × 300 kg = 1,800 kg | $30,333/kg | $14,667/kg | 1.00× |
   | **H1 2026** | ≥10 orbital of 12 × 300 kg = **250 kg** | **$36,800/kg** | **$19,600/kg** | **≥1.20×** |
   | H1 2026, ceiling | 12 × 300 kg = 3,600 kg | $30,667/kg | $16,333/kg | 1.00× |
   | **Q2 2025** | 5 of 5 point-in-time, **0 HASTE** = **1,500 kg** | **$26,333/kg** | **$16,667/kg** | **1.00×** |
   | Q1 2025, H1 2025, Q1 2026 | mission mix **not filed** | — | — | **UNEXERCISED** |

   **The filing-supported reconversion is 1.00×–1.50× (+0% to +50%), not 1.79×–2.62× (+79% to
   +162%).** And it is **zero in the one period whose mix is fully filed** — Q2 2025 was *"All
   five … point-in-time launches"* with no HASTE at all — so **"four of four periods" is
   falsified**: the correction applies to **one of the three periods with a filed mix**, and is
   `UNEXERCISED` in the other three.

2. **The registered band's arithmetic is not RKLB's.** `22.8 t ÷ 8.70 t = 2.621` (+162.1%) and
   `22.8 t ÷ 12.76 t = 1.787` (+78.7%) are **Falcon 9's** realized-denominator ratios — 22.8 t is
   Falcon 9's nameplate capacity, and 8.70 t / 12.76 t are SPCX's filed t-per-launch from the
   8-K Space table ([📄 SPCX 10-Q p.35](https://agentii.ai/v/SPCX/sec8/35);
   [📄 SPCX 8-K p.7](https://agentii.ai/v/SPCX/sec7/7)). 002's own ledger states the +79%/+162%
   range against those two SPCX pages. **The direction transfers to RKLB; the magnitude does
   not, and 003 entities.md line 53 carries the range on row 26's attribution. This artifact
   reports the row as a mis-attribution of an SPCX ratio range onto an RKLB artifact.**

3. **DA-25 is quarantine-grade on BOTH legs — and it is period-normalisation, not timing.** The
   `×N` reconstruction (disclosed per-launch × launch count) closes in **2 of the 6 periods** and
   its residual **changes sign** — negative in every 2025 period, positive in every 2026 period —
   which no `timing` shift can produce. The zero-HASTE control kills `timing` outright: at Q2
   2025, where recognition period ≡ launch period by construction for all five missions, the
   revenue leg still diverges **−15.3%** and the cost leg **−22.9%**.

**And the inversion that matters for the thesis: on the corrected denominator, RKLB's
demonstrated unit cost ROSE. Cost per launch fell 12.0% YoY ($5.0M → $4.4M per launch), but cost
per kilogram to LEO rose from $16,667/kg to $22,000/kg — +32.0% — because two of the six Q2 2026
missions bought no kilogram at all.** The disclosed improvement is a denominator artefact; the
corrected series goes the other way.

`wrong_if` under test, PIL-1's: `metric=abs_pct_change_in_demonstrated_price_per_kg_to_LEO_after_denominator_validation`,

than on the ceiling one:**

| basis A per kg, Q2 2025 → Q2 2026 | change | ±15% |
|---|---|---|
| ceiling denominator (300 kg both periods) | $26,333/kg → $30,333/kg = **+15.2%** | breaches by **0.2 pp** — marginal |

| **B** — marginal cost per launch | disclosed cost per launch $4.4M ÷ 300 kg | **$14,667/kg** (ceiling) · **$22,000/kg** (mix-corrected) | **DEMONSTRATED** |
| **C** — fully loaded amortised | **unconstructible** — §3.2 | — | filing-cited absence |

> Electron transaction price of $9.1M. Quoted bare it would read as Electron price strength. It
> is a three-vehicle basket whose largest future member has never flown, and its count is a
> `CLAIMED` "90-plus" with no filed denominator. It is carried here only with that contaminant
> named.

### 3.2 Basis C is a filing-cited structural absence

Not a research shortfall. The issuer says, in the segment note, verbatim:

> *"Management does not regularly review either reporting segment's total assets or operating
> expenses. This is because in general, the Company's long-lived assets, facilities, and
> equipment are shared by each reporting segment."*
> — [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.33](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/33)

Basis C needs segment-level assets and operating expense to amortise a vehicle across the
program. RKLB states that this allocation **is not produced and is not reviewed**. Basis C is
therefore **structurally absent at RKLB** and stays absent: no derivable substitute exists,
because the shared-asset statement is the issuer telling you the split does not exist as an
accounting object. Disposition class: `UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES`. The specific
disclosure that would resolve it is a segment asset and operating-expense schedule — which the
issuer has affirmatively declined to maintain.

Cross-check that the segment note *does* carry everything else, so this is an absence of one
thing and not of the note:
Launch Services revenue $44,586 + Space Systems $189,480 = **$234,066** = filed total revenues;
H1: $108,249 + $326,165 = **$434,414** = filed total revenues. Products $— / Services $44,586 for
Launch Services: **the segment is 100% services revenue**
([📄 RKLB 10-Q p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32);
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.33](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/33);
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/6)).

### 3.3 The per-launch series — six disclosed points, DEMONSTRATED

Disclosed cost and revenue per launch, with the spread. Every row is a filed figure; the spread
column is arithmetic on filed cells.

| Period | launches | rev/launch | cost/launch | spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2025 | 5 | **$7.1M** | **$5.7M** | $1.4M |
| Q2 2025 | 5 | **$7.9M** | **$5.0M** | $2.9M |
| H1 2025 | 10 | **$7.5M** | **$5.3M** | $2.2M |
| Q1 2026 | 6 | **$9.3M** | **$5.4M** | $3.9M |
| Q2 2026 | 6 | **$9.1M** | **$4.4M** | **$4.7M** |
| H1 2026 | 12 | **$9.2M** | **$4.9M** | $4.3M |

Q1 2026 and Q1 2025 figures: [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec104/31).
Q2 2026/2025 and H1 2026/2025 and the HASTE count:
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37).
FY series: **$8.5M / $4.8M** (FY2025), **$7.8M / $5.7M** (FY2024), **$7.1M / $7.0M** (FY2023),
with the FY2023 cost figure filed as excluding a $2.1M retention-credit benefit and a $4.1M
contract-loss-reversal benefit ([📄 RKLB 10-K p.46](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/46)).

**The spread widens in every period along the quarterly path — $1.4M → $2.9M → $3.9M → $4.7M —
a 3.4× widening.** The filing attributes the movement to *"changes in customer mix and mission
complexity during the period in which the launches occurred"*, **not** to list-price increases,
and files the list-price decoupling explicitly:

> *"Growth rates between launches and total launch service revenue are not perfectly correlated
> because our total revenue is affected by other variables, such as the revenue per launch, which
> can vary considerably based on factors such as unique orbit and insertion requirements, payload
> handling needs, launch location, time sensitivity of mission completion, method of revenue
> recognition and other factors."*
> — [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37)

**So the series is not a price curve and must not be plotted as one.** It is a mix-and-complexity
series whose own disclosure says so.

> ⚠️ **Two traps, registered.** (1) Q1 2025's revenue per launch `$7.1M` is **filed natively** on
> [📄 p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec104/31) — 002's table reached the same value by
> derivation (H1 − Q2) and labelled it `DERIVED`. The value agrees; the grade does not, and the
> native filing is the stronger one. (2) That same `$7.1M` is **numerically identical to FY2023's
> filed revenue per launch**, on a different period and a different launch count. A series built
> by eyeballing `$7.1M` rows will silently splice a quarter and a year.

### 3.4 DA-25, leg 1 — the revenue normalisation, and the stability test

**The construction.** Revenue per launch × launches, against the audited Launch Services revenue
line. Segment revenue from [📄 p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32); Q1 2025 and Q1 2026
segment revenue derived as H1 − Q2 from those filed cells (H1 2025 $82,238 − Q2 2025 $46,646 =
$35,592; H1 2026 $108,249 − Q2 2026 $44,586 = $63,663).

Divergence is stated on the brief's convention — **(`×N` construction − filed) ÷ filed** — so a
negative value means the construction **understates** the audited line and a positive value means
it **overstates** it.

| Period | N × rev/launch | filed segment revenue | divergence | % of filed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2025 | 5 × $7.1M = $35,500k | $35,592k | **−$92k** | −0.26% |
| Q2 2025 | 5 × $7.9M = $39,500k | $46,646k | **−$7,146k** | **−15.32%** |
| H1 2025 | 10 × $7.5M = $75,000k | $82,238k | −$7,238k | −8.80% |
| Q1 2026 | 6 × $9.3M = $55,800k | $63,663k | −$7,863k | −12.35% |
| Q2 2026 | 6 × $9.1M = $54,600k | $44,586k | **+$10,014k** | **+22.46%** |
| H1 2026 | 12 × $9.2M = $110,400k | $108,249k | +$2,151k | +1.99% |

**The stability test, run in all six periods, exactly as the brief requires: it is QUARANTINED.**

- **It closes (within ±5%) in 2 of 6 periods** — Q1 2025 (−0.26%) and H1 2026 (+1.99%).
- **It breaches ±15% in 2 of 6** — Q2 2025 (−15.32%) and **Q2 2026 (+22.46%)**, the registered
  "22.5% gap" — and ±5% in **4 of 6**.
- **The residual changes SIGN.** Negative in all three 2025 rows, positive in both 2026 quarters.
  **A construction that closes at one period and fails at the next is a coincidence, not a
  mechanism**, and here it does worse than fail — it reverses.

**And the sign reversal is falsified by a filed directional statement, not merely by tolerance.**
The only filed term the residual could be is *other launch revenue* — the disclosed metric is
*"the average transaction price attributable to launch contract performance obligations"*, which
by construction excludes it. The filing says of that very term, in the very quarter the residual
needs it to be **−$10,014k**:

> *"The decrease was partially offset by **increased** other launch revenue of $5.7 million, which
> includes contract termination and study revenue."*
> — [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37)

**It cannot both increase by $5.7M and be −$10.0M.** The construction is refuted by a filed
statement of direction, and the refutation is independent of any tolerance choice.

**A second, independent refutation, in the opposite direction.** The same page files the YoY
Launch Services movement as a **decrease of $2.1M** in launch revenue, of which other launch
revenue contributed +$5.7M — so launch-contract revenue **fell $7.8M** YoY. The `×N` construction
requires it to have **risen $15.1M** ($39.5M → $54.6M). **A $22.9M YoY discrepancy, signed
against the filing.**

**The mechanism is period-normalisation.** The disclosed metric's numerator is allocated **to the
period in which the launch occurs**, *"regardless of whether the revenue is recognized using the
point-in-time or over-time method"*; the segment revenue line is what was **recognised** in the
period. For over-time HASTE missions the two are different objects: the full transaction price of
six missions lands in the `×6` construction, while the segment line carries only the recognised
portion, *"a significant portion of [HASTE] revenue [having] already been recognized in prior
periods under the overtime accounting method"* ([📄 RKLB Q2 2026 call p.2](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/ect21/2)).
**Launch-period allocation ÷ recognition-period revenue is period-normalisation, and it is
unbounded in sign.**

**`timing` is FALSIFIED, and the control is filed.** Q2 2025 is the zero-HASTE control: *"All five
Electron launch missions completed for the three months ended June 30, 2025 were point-in-time
launches."* Every mission's launch period ≡ its recognition period, so a pure timing wedge must
vanish. It does not:

| Q2 2025, zero-HASTE control | constructed (`×N`) | filed | divergence |
|---|---|---|---|
| revenue leg | $39,500k | $46,646k | **−15.3%** |
| cost leg | $25,000k | $32,426k | **−22.9%** |

**Both legs diverge at the control. The `timing` hypothesis is dead; period-normalisation is the
mechanism, and it is a property of the metric's definition, not of when cash landed.**

### 3.5 DA-25, leg 2 — the margin leg

Disclosed cost/launch ÷ disclosed revenue/launch, against the audited segment gross margin. Both
legs of the defect, on one table.

| Period | disclosed implied GM | audited segment GM | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2025 | 19.72% | 20.28% | −0.56 pp |
| Q2 2025 | 36.71% | 30.48% | +6.23 pp |
| H1 2025 | 29.33% | 26.07% | +3.26 pp |
| Q1 2026 | 41.94% | 44.33% | −2.39 pp |
| **Q2 2026** | **51.65%** | **42.86%** | **+8.79 pp** |
| H1 2026 | 46.74% | 43.73% | +3.01 pp |

Q2 2026 is the registered pair — **51.6% disclosed vs 42.9% audited, an 8.7 pp gap** — and it is
the widest of the six, not the typical one. **The margin leg is not stable either: it changes sign
(−0.56 pp, −2.39 pp).** A margin series that is +6.2, −2.4 and +8.8 points away from its own
audited segment table on successive periods is a normalisation, not a measurement.

**But the two legs are not symmetric in the same period** — Q2 2026 revenue leg **+22.5%** against
cost leg **+3.6%** ($26,400k constructed vs $25,476k filed), on the convention above. That asymmetry is PIL-5's finding in one
line: **the per-launch disclosure is a substantially better cost-side measurement than revenue-side
one, and the revenue side is unreconciled.**

### 3.6 DA-23 — the sign test, run on the component identity

**Served value:** `us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss` = **+57,514,000 USD** for the three months ended
2026-06-30. **Filed value:** **$(57,514)$ thousand** — magnitude identical, sign stripped.

**The component identity, in-line, with the opex definition named:**

```
  gross profit      84,576   (filed, [📄 p.6])
− total operating expenses  142,090  (filed = R&D, net 82,429 + SG&A 59,661)
= operating loss   (57,514)  (filed)                          ← closes EXACTLY
```

**Opex definition used: `Total operating expenses` as filed on the face of the condensed
consolidated statements of operations** — R&D, net plus SG&A. It is the **exclusive** definition.

**Why the inclusive definition is inadmissible here, shown in-line rather than asserted:** pairing
gross profit with `us-gaap:CostsAndExpenses` double-counts cost of revenues —
`84,576 − (149,490 + 142,090) = −207,004` — which is **not** the filed figure. The admissible
pairing is `revenue − CostsAndExpenses = 234,066 − 291,580 = −57,514`, or equivalently
`gross profit − total operating expenses = −57,514`. Both close; the mixed pairing does not.
Source: [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.6](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/6).

**Scope of the strip — larger than the register records.** The served `OperatingIncomeLoss` is
positive in **12 of 12 periods sampled** (Q2 2026 +57,514,000; H1 2026 +113,483,000; Q1 2026
+55,969,000; Q3 2025 +58,969,000; 9M 2025 +177,796,000; Q2 2025 +59,639,000; H1 2025
+118,827,000; Q1 2025 +59,188,000; FY2025 +228,838,000; 9M 2024 +138,252,000; Q3 2024
+51,899,000; FY2024 +189,801,000). RKLB has no positive operating income in its history, so
**all 12 are strips**, not one. **And the detector is the identity and nothing else:** because
every period is negative, the strip is invisible to any sign-plausibility heuristic and invisible
in every period-over-period comparison — differences and ratios are all correctly signed. `EPS ×
shares` is inadmissible as a substitute and doubly so at RKLB: weighted-average shares moved
515,086,631 → 629,681,803, **+22.2%**, so the product moves for a capital-structure reason (DA-28)
unrelated to the sign.

### 3.7 The F5 floor — F5c for Electron, F5b for Neutron

**Electron is F5c — FULLY EXPENDABLE.** Verified, not inherited. The 10-K files the vehicle as
*"two primary stages and an innovative third kick stage, standing at 18 meters tall, with a
diameter of 1.2 meters and a lift-off mass of approximately 14,000 kg"*
([📄 RKLB 10-K p.7](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/7)) — no recovery system, no recovered stage.
Recovery appears only as a **capability statement about the future**: *"the **potential ability**
to successfully recover a stage from space, **providing a path to** reusability"*
([📄 RKLB 10-Q p.34](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/34)). A path to reusability is not
reusability. **F5b would require a reusable first stage; Electron has none, and none has flown
recovered.**

| tier | vehicle | architecture | floor | grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F5a** | — | none at RKLB | **ABSENT** | resolving source: a propellant-floor disclosure; none exists for any RKLB vehicle |
| **F5b** | **Neutron** | partially reusable (*"will feature a reusable first stage"*) | expended upper stage + recovered booster amortisation; ≈**13,000 kg** to LEO in reusable configuration | **MODELED** — never flown; ASP guidance `$50M–$55M` per launch [📄 call p.3](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/ect21/3) is `CLAIMED` |
| **F5c** | **Electron** | **fully expendable** | **whole-vehicle manufacturing floor** | **DEMONSTRATED** |

**Only F5c is DEMONSTRATED, and Electron is the only RKLB vehicle in it.** The demonstrated
whole-vehicle floor is the cost-per-launch series — **$7.0M (FY2023) → $5.7M (FY2024) → $4.8M
(FY2025) → $4.4M (Q2 2026)** — falling while cadence rose 10 → 16 → 21 → 12 launches. That is a
real cost curve, and it is the only one in the universe. **On the corrected denominator it does
not survive** (§3.8). Neutron's floor is F5b and is MODELED: it is forward, unflown, and its
payload figure is a design target. **PIL-4's Neutron case therefore rests on F5b, not F5a** — and
at RKLB no F5a vehicle exists at all, which this artifact records as an absence with its resolving
source rather than as a coverage claim.

> **The registered inversion, restated with RKLB's instance.** The sector's cost conversation runs
> on the architectures whose floor is unproven (F5a, F5b) while F5c holds the only demonstrated
> price. At RKLB the two are the *same company, one quarter apart*: the unproven tier is the one
> being marketed and guided, the proven tier is the one being disclosed per launch.

### 3.8 The RECONVERSION — corrected values, with basis

**The denominator the filing supports.**

| candidate denominator | filed at RKLB? | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **300 kg, LEO** | **yes, twice, as `up to`** — [📄 p.7](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/7), [📄 p.8](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/8) | **CEILING. Admissible only as a floor-of-$/kg.** |
| **300 kg × non-HASTE missions** | **yes** — mission counts and the HASTE mix filed [📄 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) | **ADMISSIBLE.** The only filing-supported realized adjustment. |
| mass-to-orbit (kg actually lifted) | **no — no period** | **ABSENT.** RKLB files a spacecraft *count* (*"over 250 spacecraft to orbit … across 87 successful missions"*, [📄 p.34](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/34)), never a mass. |
| SSO-specific (~200 kg) | **no** | **WITHDRAWN** — and contradicted by the filed 300 kg across 38–120°. |

**Corrected values.**

| period | basis | denominator | basis A | basis B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Q2 2026** | revenue / cost per launch, 4 orbital of 6 | 200 kg | **$45,500/kg** | **$22,000/kg** |
| Q2 2026 | ceiling | 300 kg | $30,333/kg | $14,667/kg |
| **H1 2026** | 10 orbital of 12 (HASTE ≥2, unbounded) | 250 kg | **$36,800/kg** | **$19,600/kg** |
| H1 2026 | ceiling | 300 kg | $30,667/kg | $16,333/kg |
| **Q2 2025** | 5 of 5 point-in-time, 0 HASTE | 300 kg | **$26,333/kg** | **$16,667/kg** |
| Q1 2025 / H1 2025 / Q1 2026 | mix not filed | — | `UNEXERCISED` | `UNEXERCISED` |

Every value: arithmetic on filed cells → **figures DEMONSTRATED, division MODELED** where the
per-mission mass is the ceiling.

**Bounds and their directions, stated so neither is over-read.** Excluding HASTE from the
denominator while keeping its revenue in the numerator makes the corrected figure an **upper
bound** of the true $/kg. Assuming each orbital mission flew the full 300 kg makes it a **lower
bound**. HASTE revenue is not separately filed — *"revenue was recognized over time and was
partially recognized in prior quarters"* — so the bound cannot be tightened from public filings.
The corrected figure is exact if the four Q2 2026 orbital missions each flew 300 kg.

**Against the inherited correction.**

| | register (entities.md L53, ledger row 26) | this artifact, from the filing |
|---|---|---|
| multiplier | **1.79×–2.62×** | **1.00×–1.50×** |
| restatement | **+79% to +162%** | **+0% to +50%** |
| periods | **four of four** | **one of three with a filed mix** (Q2 2026); `UNEXERCISED` in Q1 2025, H1 2025, Q1 2026; **zero** in Q2 2025 |
| source of the range | — | `22.8 t ÷ 8.70 t = 2.621` and `22.8 t ÷ 12.76 t = 1.787` — **Falcon 9's** realized denominators, cited in ledger §1.6.1 to [📄 SPCX 10-Q p.35](https://agentii.ai/v/SPCX/sec8/35) and [📄 SPCX 8-K p.7](https://agentii.ai/v/SPCX/sec7/7) |

**The direction is right and it is the important half of the correction: a `up to` ceiling in the
denominator produces a floor of the true $/kg, so 001's figures are too low.** The magnitude is
SPCX's, and "four of four periods" is falsified at RKLB by the filed zero-HASTE control.

**The corrected series goes the wrong way, and this is the artifact's second headline.**
Cost **per launch** fell 12.0% YoY ($5.0M → $4.4M). Cost **per kilogram to LEO** rose:

| | Q2 2025 | Q2 2026 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost per launch | $5.0M | $4.4M | **−12.0%** |
| kg denominator (orbital missions × 300 kg) | 1,500 kg | 1,200 kg | −20.0% |
| **cost per kg, basis B** | **$16,667/kg** | **$22,000/kg** | **+32.0%** |

The rise holds unless Q2 2025's missions averaged more than ~24% *less* filled than Q2 2026's — the
break-even is a fill-rate ratio of 0.758. **Two of six missions bought no kilogram, and the
disclosure reports the cost side as though they had.** For `PIL-3`, the single observed step in
the universe's cost curve is a **denominator artefact in the optimistic direction**: on the
validated denominator, RKLB's demonstrated unit cost improved by nothing and worsened by a third.

| RKLB 10-Q, filed 2026-08-10 (`sec109`) | p.6, p.32, p.33, p.34, p.36, p.37 | income statement; segment tables; the basis-C quote; the 87-mission / 250-spacecraft count; the per-launch series; the HASTE mix; the metric definitions verbatim |
| RKLB 10-Q, filed 2026-05-xx (`sec104`) | p.31 | Q1 2026 and **Q1 2025** per-launch figures, filed natively |
| RKLB 10-K, filed 2026-02-26 (`sec87`) | p.5, p.7, p.8, p.46 | the 300 kg ceiling and the 38–120° envelope; Electron's stage architecture; Neutron's 13,000 kg and reusable first stage; the FY per-launch series and backlog |
| RKLB Q2 2026 earnings call (`ect21`) | p.1–p.4 | segment revenue commentary; gross-margin bridge; backlog composition; Neutron ASP guidance ($50M–$55M) and the 1-3-5 ramp; the over-time HASTE recognition statement |

**Out of scope by rule.** `get_segment_data` (raises `column "k" does not exist`; double-counts)
and `data_freshness` (reports 2027-04-12) were not used. No figure was sourced from a linkbase
`LABEL`.

**Scope limit that is a finding, not an omission.** RKLB's FY2023–FY2025 per-launch series carries
the same HASTE contamination as the quarterlies, and the HASTE mission counts for those years were
**not located in the pages read** → the FY series is quoted on the ceiling basis with the
adjustment `UNEXERCISED`, not assumed to be zero.

**Coverage gate.** RKLB is covered for 10-K/10-Q/8-K and earnings transcripts across the six
periods above; all six per-launch points and all four segment-table periods were read at source.

---

## 5. Mode: retrieval-strategy

The sequence that produced §3, and what each step was for.

1. **Locate the unit — the metric definitions, not the metrics.** `read_source_outline` on the
   Q2 2026 10-Q, then `read_source_pages` on p.34–p.37. **The definitions are what make the leg
   decidable**: *"Revenue per launch represents the average transaction price attributable to
   launch contract performance obligations during the period in which the launch occurs,
   regardless of whether the revenue is recognized using the point-in-time or over-time method"*
   is the sentence that converts a 22.5% "gap" into a named mechanism. **Retrieval rule: for a
   normalised per-unit metric, read the definition page before the number page.**
2. **Read the face, not the extract.** `read_source_pages` on p.6 for the income statement, so
   the DA-23 sign test runs on filed cells with the opex definition visible in the same table.
   The served XBRL fact was then queried separately (`search_xbrl_facts
   concept=OperatingIncomeLoss`, 12 periods) **only to size the strip** — never as the value.
3. **Get the denominator from the same page as the numerator.** The HASTE mix (p.37) sits on the
   same page as the per-launch figures, so no cross-document join is needed for the reconversion.
   **Where a numerator and its denominator live on the same page, use it — every cross-page join
   is a place a period label can slip.**
4. **Test the denominator against the filing's own envelope.** `search_keyword_in_source "kg"` on
   the 10-K returned p.5, p.7, p.8, p.44 — the 300 kg and the 38–120°/38–60° envelope, both filed
   with the capacity sentence. **That is what withdrew 002's SSO channel**: a single 300 kg figure
   spanning an envelope that contains the SSO band cannot also have a lower SSO figure.
5. **What returned zero, and what that means.** `search_keyword_in_source "payload"` on the Q2
   10-Q returns three pages — p.34, p.36, p.37 — and **none carries a payload mass**; the 10-K's
   `kg` hits are capacity, mass, and lift-off mass only. **A zero from a keyword search is
   evidence about the query; a zero from a concept query is evidence about the tag** (ledger item
   29). The conclusion "RKLB files no realized mass-to-orbit" therefore rests on reading every
   page the keyword surfaces, not on the zero.
6. **Re-read the load-bearing pages at the end.** p.32 and p.33 were read twice, after all
   arithmetic was done, to verify the segment figures and to capture the basis-C quote verbatim.
   **The second read is where the segment-to-consolidated ties were confirmed** ($44,586 +
   $189,480 = $234,066; $108,249 + $326,165 = $434,414; services $44,586 + $8,133 = $52,719).

**Strategy lesson carried forward.** At RKLB the defect was found by **construction failure**
(§3.4), not by mislabelled data: every filed cell involved is correctly labelled and correctly
signed. A retrieval strategy that hunts for wrong labels finds nothing here. The only way in is to
**rebuild the issuer's own metric from its own components in every period and watch it fail**.

---

## 6. What this could not resolve

**Class throughout: `UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES`.** None of these is a platform defect —
the platform served each filed cell faithfully, including the DA-23 sign, which is a *detected*
strip with the identity as its detector.

| unresolved | why | the specific disclosure that would resolve it |
|---|---|---|
| **The realized $/kg — the metric the whole thesis calibrates on** | RKLB files no mass-to-orbit in any period, and files its one mass as a ceiling. The corrected figure is exact only under the assumption that each orbital mission flew 300 kg. | an Electron **mass-to-orbit** metric, defined in DA-07's terms as the summed verified payload mass of successful missions — i.e. what SPCX files and RKLB does not |
| **H1 2026's HASTE count** | filed as ≥2 and unbounded; the 12 launches and the per-launch figures are filed, the split is not | the H1 HASTE mission count — the Q2 count is filed, the Q1 count is not |
| **Q1 2025, H1 2025, Q1 2026 corrections** | mix not filed in either 10-Q | a per-period HASTE mission count covering FY2025 and Q1 2026 |
| **Basis C** | the issuer states the allocation is not produced and not reviewed | a segment asset and operating-expense schedule — affirmatively declined |
| **Basis A′ as an Electron price** | the only backlog-implied ASP available is a three-vehicle basket on a `CLAIMED` count | a filed launch-services backlog with a launch count on the same basis and date |
| **DA-26 at RKLB** | `UNEXERCISED`, not clean: the sampled XBRL facts carry self-consistent durations (FY and nine-month durations appear as their own facts), so the defect could only live in a slot/label layer this artifact did not read | a slot-level audit of the extracted metrics layer |
| **DA-27 at RKLB** | **vacuous, not clean**: fiscal year end month 12 against calendar quarters means the label cannot be wrong | — the test cannot fail, so its passing carries no information |

**PRESENCE vs ABSENCE, recorded explicitly.** Three tests here did not run and are therefore not
passed: DA-27 (**vacuous** — no information), DA-26 (**unexercised** at fact level), and the
DA-25 stability test in the three periods whose mission mix is unfiled (**unexercised**). The
DA-23 component identity, the DA-25 stability test in all six observable periods, and the
segment-to-consolidated ties **did** run, and all three results are reported as they came out.

**One thing this artifact will not do: re-raise the F5 coverage gap.** F5 is split three ways and
the tiers are exhaustive. What RKLB contributes is the instance, not a claim.
````

````markdown
# RKLB × operational-kpi — the per-launch series, and its failure to reconcile to the audited segment table

## 0. The finding

**The `revenue per launch` / `cost per launch` series does not reconcile to the audited segment
table, in most periods, on either leg — and the `× mission-count` construction that would make
it do so is `QUARANTINED`. It FAILS the mandatory stability test.**

The brief's headline reconciliation reproduces arithmetically: `$9.1M × 6 = $54,600k` against a
filed Launch Services revenue of `$44,586k` is a **+22.46%** overstatement
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) ·
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32). That is not the finding. The finding is
that **this construction closes in some periods and fails in others, changes the sign of its own
error twice inside four quarters, and has never closed outside the metric's own rounding band
after Q1 2025.** Under the brief's own rule — *a construction that closes at one period and fails
at the next is a coincidence, not a mechanism* — the construction is **not admissible as a
derivation of the audited segment table.**

**Corrections to claims carried into this task, established here by arithmetic on the filings:**

| Claim as received | Verdict | What the arithmetic gives |
|---|---|---|
| The six reported per-launch points `(Q1 25 $7.1/$5.7 · Q2 25 $7.9/$5.0 · H1 25 $7.5/$5.3 · Q1 26 $9.3/$5.4 · Q2 26 $9.1/$4.4 · H1 26 $9.2/$4.9)` | **REPRODUCES, 6 of 6, exact** | Every one is filed verbatim; no correction needed. **Four more interim points and three annual points are also filed** and are added in §1 |
| The spread widens **every** period, `$1.4M → $4.7M` | **NOT AS WRITTEN** | The chronological sequence is `0.1 / 2.1 / 1.7 / 2.0 / 2.0 / 2.1 / 1.4 / 2.9 / 2.2 / 4.2 / 3.7 / 3.9 / 4.7 / 4.3` ($M) — it narrows twice. It widens on **every like-for-like comparison except Q1**, and on every annual comparison (§1.3) |
| The **Launch − Space** segment-margin differential is positive in **every** period | **FALSE** | Negative in **4 of 14** observable periods — FY2023 (−13.88 pp), Q1 2025 (−11.95 pp), Q2 2025 (−2.39 pp), H1 2025 (−6.50 pp). Positive in 10 of 14 (§6) |
| The **cost-side** gap exceeds 5% in **4 of 6** periods | **3 of 6 — the legs are swapped** | Cost-side: +0.44 / −22.90 / −12.83 / −8.58 / +3.63 / −3.47% → exceeds 5% in **3**. **Revenue**-side: −0.26 / −15.32 / −8.80 / −12.35 / +22.46 / +1.99% → exceeds 5% in **4**. The brief's count is right for the revenue leg (§4.2) |
| `8.7 pp` margin gap | **Rounds correctly; the exact value is 8.79 pp** | `51.648% − 42.861% = 8.79 pp`; 8.7 is the difference of the already-rounded operands (§3.2) |

**The mechanism is period-normalisation, and `timing` is NOT reinstated.** The construction was
tested against the one competing basis the filings permit — a point-in-time-only scope, which the
Q2 2025 10-Q states in its own words — and it **fails on that basis too** (+44.82% in Q2 2026,
+18.37% in H1 2026). No single basis closes the series. That, and not a recognition lag, is what
makes this a normalisation (§5).

**One item is `UNRESOLVABLE-FROM-PUBLIC-SOURCES`, and the frontmatter flag scopes to it alone:**
the metric's own numerator-and-denominator construction is never disclosed (§16). **The `×N`
falsifier WAS exercised and it FAILED — flagging the construction as unresolvable does not soften
that result.** A construction whose terms cannot be located is uninformative whether or not it
closes; this one fails on the arithmetic as well.

---

## 1. The series as disclosed — every period available

### 1.1 The metric as filed, with its definitions

The metric is issuer-defined, disclosed in the MD&A key-metrics block, and stated to the nearest
`$0.1M`. **Its definition is not stable across filings** — three distinct wordings are filed:

| Filing | Filed wording of the numerator |
|---|---|
| Q1 2025 10-Q [📄 p.27](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec101/27) | "**Revenue value per launch** represents the average **revenue per launch contract** attributable to **launches that occurred** during a period, **regardless of when the revenue was recognized**." |
| Q2 2025 10-Q [📄 p.30](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec102/30) | "Revenue value per launch represents the average revenue per launch contract attributable to **point-in-time launches** that occurred during a period." ← **narrowest** |
| Q3 2025 10-Q onward — [📄 sec103 p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec103/31) · [📄 sec104 p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec104/31) · [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) · FY2025 10-K [📄 p.46](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/46) | "Revenue per launch represents the average **transaction price** attributable to **launch contract performance obligations during the period in which the launch occurs**, regardless of whether the revenue is recognized using the point-in-time or over-time method of revenue recognition." |

**The cost leg's construction is filed, and it is not the segment's cost line.** Q2 2026, verbatim:
*"Cost per launch is calculated by taking **actual costs of the launch vehicles that occur in the
period**, regardless of whether the costs were recognized using the point-in-time or over-time
method and **all period costs in the period of launch**."*
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37). *"All period costs"* is defined nowhere —
it is not the Launch Services cost of revenues line, and §4.2 measures the difference. The Q2 2025
10-Q [📄 p.30](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec102/30) files a revenue-leg definition and no cost-leg
definition.

Two things follow, and both are load-bearing. **(a)** The noun changed: `revenue per launch contract`
(Q1 2025) became `transaction price attributable to launch contract performance obligations` (Q3 2025
onward). A transaction price is a contract value; it has no reason to equal a period's recognised
revenue and is dimensionally free to exceed it — which, at Q2 2026, it does (§4.4). **(b)** The cost
leg is defined explicitly in Q1 2025 and from Q3 2025 onward, but **Q2 2025's page defines only the
revenue leg** — the cost-per-launch basis is unstated in that filing
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.30](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec102/30).

The issuer's own caution is filed and is repeated verbatim in every period: the metric
*"may not provide absolute clarity with regards to pricing and competitive dynamics in the
marketplace"*, and its variability drivers are enumerated as *"unique orbit and insertion
requirements, payload handling needs, launch location, time sensitivity of mission completion,
**method of revenue recognition** and other factors"*
[📄 RKLB 10-K p.46](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/46). That list is a disclosure about the
metric's construction, not an explanation of any gap asserted here.

as any other point in the series**: it *"excludes a $2.1 million benefit from non-recurring employee
retention credit to Launch Services cost of revenue and a $4.1 million benefit from non-recurring
reversal of provision made for contract losses that were credited to Launch Services cost of
revenue"* [📄 RKLB 10-K p.46](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/46). Two named exclusions appear at
FY2023 and nowhere else — a definitional discontinuity **inside** the series, before any
reconciliation is attempted.

### 1.3 The spread: corrected

`Rev/launch − cost/launch`, chronological, `$M`: `0.1 → 2.1 → 1.7 → 2.0 → 2.0 → 2.1 → 1.4 → 2.9 →
2.2 → 4.2 → 3.7 → 3.9 → 4.7 → 4.3`.

- **Not monotone.** It narrows at Q1 2024 → Q2 2024 (`2.1 → 1.7`). The apparent narrowings at
  `Q2 2025 → H1 2025` (`2.9 → 2.2`) and `Q3 2025 → FY2025` (`4.2 → 3.7`) are **period-length
  artefacts** — the longer period *contains* the shorter one, so those two pairs are not
  comparable and I do not count them either way.
- **Widens on every like-for-like comparison, with one exception.** Q2: `1.7 → 2.9 → 4.7`;
  H1: `2.0 → 2.2 → 4.3`; Annual: `0.1 → 2.1 → 3.7`. **Q1 is the exception**: `2.1 → 1.4 → 3.9` —
  it narrows in 2025 before widening in 2026.
- The brief's `$1.4M → $4.7M` is a Q1 2025 → Q2 2026 span across five intervening periods. As a
  **like-for-like year-over-year** statement it is correct and durable; as a monotonicity claim it
  is not.
- **The widening is driven by both legs, not by price alone.** Revenue per launch rose
  `$7.1M → $9.1M` (`+28.2%`) between Q1 2025 and Q2 2026 while cost per launch *fell*
  `$5.7M → $4.4M` (`−22.8%`). The cost leg contributes more of the widening than the revenue leg
  does in Q2 2026 (`$1.3M` of the `$3.3M` increase, on a same-period-length comparison).
- **Attribution is the issuer's, and it is not a list-price claim.** Filed verbatim: *"The increase
  in revenue per launch reflects changes in customer mix and mission complexity during the period in
  which the launches occurred."* [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) ·
  [📄 sec104 p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec104/31). **CLAIMED.** No list-price increase is
  asserted by the issuer, and none is asserted here.

### 1.4 Internal consistency of the annual point — a new check

The FY2025 10-K gives an annual metric and the 10-Qs give three quarters of the same year. If the
metric were a count-weighted period average, the annual figure should decompose into the quarters.
It does not, cleanly. **DERIVED** (arithmetic on filed cells; rounding band propagated):

| | Rev/launch | Cost/launch |
|---|---|---|
| FY2025 as filed, × 21 launches | `$8.5M × 21 = $178.5M ± $1.05M` | `$4.8M × 21 = $100.8M ± $1.05M` |
| Nine months to Sep 30 2025 (Q1 + Q2 + Q3) | `35.5 + 39.5 + 40.4 = $115.4M ± $0.7M` | `28.5 + 25.0 + 23.6 = $77.1M ± $0.7M` |
| **Implied Q4 2025** (residual ÷ 7 launches) | **`≈ $9.0M ± $0.25M`** | **`≈ $3.4M ± $0.25M`** |

The implied Q4 2025 **cost per launch of `$3.4M ± $0.25M` lies below every one of the eleven
disclosed interim values** (minimum disclosed: `$4.4M`, Q2 2026) — by `30%`. Two readings survive:
a genuine step-change in Q4 2025 that the company never disclosed in a quarterly filing, or a
metric whose period constructions are **not additive**. I cannot separate them, because **no Q4
10-Q exists** — and that is itself the point: this check runs entirely on filed cells, assumes
nothing about the denominator beyond the filed mission count, and still fails to close. It is
independent corroboration of §4.

Three properties of this denominator matter more than its values:

1. **It counts suborbital missions.** *"Two of the six Electron launch missions completed for the
   three months ended June 30, 2026 were Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron
   ("HASTE") launch missions, for which revenue was recognized over time and was partially
   recognized in prior quarters."* [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37). The
   denominator is therefore **1/3 suborbital in Q2 2026**, while the numerator's treatment of those
   same missions is explicitly partial.
2. **The cumulative count is on the same mixed basis** — *"We have successfully launched Electron
   87 times delivering over 250 spacecraft to orbit, including suborbital launches, through June 30, 2026."*
   [📄 RKLB 10-Q p.36](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/36) — so it too cannot be compared to a
   purely orbital count without restatement.
3. **The issuer never states that this count is the metric's denominator.** The count and the metric
   appear in **different paragraphs of the same page**, with no reconciling sentence between them
   [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37). **This — an ASSIGNMENT, not a number — is
   the term that appears nowhere in any source, and it is what §3's DA-29 test turns on.**

A count is a defensible denominator only if the metric's numerator is the period's total revenue for
those same missions. §4 tests exactly that, and it is false in 6 of 14 periods.

## 3. The DA-25 reconciliation, both legs, to the audited segment table

The audited table is the segment note, whose policy is filed: *"For contracts with customers that
contain both space systems and launch services elements, revenues for each reporting segment are
generally allocated based upon the overall costs incurred for each of the reporting segments in
comparison to total overall costs of the contract."*
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32). **The metric is issuer-defined; the
segment table is audited. Where they diverge, the segment table governs every margin claim and the
metric governs only itself** (DA-25 remedy).

### 3.1 Revenue leg — Q2 2026

| Term | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue per launch, Q2 2026 | `$9.1M` | [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) |
| Launch missions, Q2 2026 | `6` | [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) |
| Construction | `$9.1M × 6 = $54,600k` | derived |
| Launch Services revenue, Q2 2026, as filed | `$44,586k` | [📄 sec109 p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32) |
| **Gap** | **`+$10,014k = +22.46%`** (`54,600 / 44,586 − 1`) | **DEMONSTRATED** |

This is the brief's `22.5%`, reproduced to the rounding of its operands.

### 3.2 Margin leg — Q2 2026

| Basis | Launch gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Implied by the issuer metric** | `(9.1 − 4.4) / 9.1 = 51.648% → 51.6%` | [📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) |
| **Audited segment table** | `19,110 / 44,586 = 42.861% → 42.9%` | [📄 sec109 p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32) |
| **Gap** | **`8.79 pp`** (exact); `8.7 pp` is the difference of the rounded operands | **DEMONSTRATED** |

### 3.3 Cost leg — Q2 2026

`$4.4M × 6 = $26,400k` against filed Launch Services **cost of revenues `$25,476k`**
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.32](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/32) → **`+$924k = +3.63%`**. The cost leg does *not*
fail at Q2 2026, and — importantly — it does not close there either: it is outside the metric's own
rounding band (§4.2).

### 3.4 Do the other legs reproduce? All three, for all six reported periods

Section 4 runs all three. Summarised here: the margin leg's implied-vs-audited gap **ranges from
`−16.48 pp` (Q3 2025) to `+8.79 pp` (Q2 2026) and flips sign five times across the 14 periods**;
only 5 of 14 periods sit within `±1 pp`, and all five are 2024/Q1 2025. **The margin-side
reconciliation fails the same stability test as the revenue-side one** — the `8.7 pp` figure is not
a bias, it is one period's draw from a distribution of period-specific divergences.

### 4.3 The results, stated plainly

1. **It does not reproduce in every period. Revenue leg: closes within `±1%` in 8 of 14 periods and
   fails in 6. Cost leg: closes within `±1%` in 6 of 14 and fails in 8.**
2. **The closes are not evidence.** Only **4 of 14** revenue-leg periods sit inside the metric's own
   rounding band, and only **6 of 14** cost-leg periods do — every one of them in 2024 or Q1 2025.
   A construction whose own precision (`±$50k × N`, i.e. up to `±$1.05M` at N = 21) exceeds the
   discrepancies it is said to explain has **never demonstrated closure beyond its own noise floor**.
   The `+0.25% / +0.24% / −0.46% / −0.26%` revenue-leg "closes" are all `≤ 0.7×` the band: they are
   **arithmetic coincidences inside the rounding**, and citing them as reconciliation would be
   exactly the failure mode DA-29 registers.
3. **The failures are far outside the band and grow.** From Q2 2025 onward the cost leg is outside
   its band in **every single period**, by `3.1×` to `32.2×`. The revenue leg is outside by up to
   `33.4×`.
4. **The error flips sign, twice, inside four quarters.** Revenue: `−12.35%` (Q1 2026) →
   `+22.46%` (Q2 2026) — a **34.8 pp** swing in one quarter. Cost: `−22.90%` (Q2 2025) →
   `+37.51%` (Q3 2025) → `−8.58%` (Q1 2026) → `+3.63%` (Q2 2026) — **60.4 pp** across two quarters
   in the first swing. **A mechanism does not do that.** A period normalisation does.
5. **The 5% threshold is not discriminable on the metric's own noise.** The metric's own
   period-to-period movement reaches `+27.9%` (rev/launch, Q2 2025 → Q3 2025) and `+18.0%`
   (cost/launch, same pair) — `3.6×` to `5.6×` the 5% criterion. A criterion smaller than the
   metric's ordinary quarterly movement cannot separate signal from movement. **The brief's
   `4 of 6` count is right for the revenue leg (`−0.26 / −15.32 / −8.80 / −12.35 / +22.46 / +1.99`),
   not the cost leg (`3 of 6`: `−22.90 / −12.83 / −8.58`).**

### 4.4 The competing basis — tested, and it fails too

The Q2 2025 10-Q files a **point-in-time-only** definition
[📄 p.30](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec102/30), and the 2026 10-Q discloses the point-in-time /
over-time split by segment [📄 sec109 p.11](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/11). That makes the
narrower scope directly testable in four periods:

| Period | `×N` ($k) | LS point-in-time revenue ($k) | Gap | LS over-time revenue ($k) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 2025 | 39,500 | 39,256 | **+0.62% — closes** | 7,390 |
| H1 2025 | 75,000 | 74,731 | **+0.36% — closes** | 7,507 |
| Q2 2026 | 54,600 | 37,703 | **+44.82% — fails** | 6,883 |
| H1 2026 | 110,400 | 93,268 | **+18.37% — fails** | 14,981 |

**So the point-in-time basis closes in 2 of 4 testable periods and fails in the other 2 — it fails
the same stability test.** It is available for 4 of 14 periods, so it is `UNEXERCISED` in the other
10; the FY recognition-model split exists at [📄 10-K p.82](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec87/82) and
was not read, which is the cheapest way to extend this. Two candidate bases, neither closing:
**that is the definition of a normalisation, and it is why the metric may not be used as a
derivation of a segment line on either basis.**

### 4.5 Scope impossibility at Q2 2026 — the sharpest single result

At Q2 2026 the construction gives `$54,600k` against **total** Launch Services revenue of
`$44,586k` — an excess of `$10,014k`. **No subset of a segment's revenue can exceed the segment
total.** Therefore **no scope re-basing whatever** — point-in-time only, over-time only, orbital
only, HASTE-excluded — can reconcile Q2 2026. The numerator is not a period revenue at all.

**And the comparator is the more generous one available.** The Launch Services revenue line is not
mission-only. Q2 2026, verbatim: the decline was *"partially offset by increased other launch
revenue of $5.7 million, which includes contract termination and study revenue"*; for the six
months: *"an increase in other launch revenue of $7.3 million, which includes contract termination
and study revenue and revenue recognized on over-time HASTE launch missions"*
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) ·
[📄 RKLB 10-Q p.42](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/42). Both are **year-over-year deltas**, so
neither yields a level to subtract — but together they establish that the audited segment line
**contains revenue attaching to no Electron mission at all**. A mission-only construction therefore
has *less* claim on that line than a total-revenue construction does, and its `+$10,014k` overshoot
is not reducible to a scope mismatch operating in the issuer's favour.

The
issuer's own wording already says so: since Q3 2025 the metric is *"the average **transaction
price** attributable to launch contract performance obligations"*
[📄 sec103 p.31](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec103/31) ·
[📄 sec109 p.37](https://agentii.ai/v/RKLB/sec109/37) — a **contract value**, which is free to
exceed a period's recognised revenue and does.

### 4.6 Verdict

> **FAILED → `QUARANTINED` on both legs.** The `revenue per launch` × mission-count construction
> reproduces the audited Launch Services segment table in some periods and not others, never
> demonstratively beyond its own rounding floor, and its error is sign-unstable. **It is not a
> mechanism and may not be used to derive, replace, or check any segment line.** The metric stands
> as an issuer-defined disclosure and as nothing else (DA-25). **The audited segment table governs.**
````
